notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's family-config/SerialDriver was replaced by a direct Driver over python_dist.CHEMYX_python.core.connect:Connection. The upstream interface is a Python object whose methods assemble a command and return a list of reply lines (connect.py:97-143), and the only parameter report is the multi-line 'view parameter' reply (connect.py:268-271); a one-command/one-reply command table cannot express that reply or keep a last-written value in the resource state. No wire syntax was changed: the driver calls the upstream methods and the fake implements only the upstream class's public methods. NOT COVERED: multi-pump mode (the setPump/addPump prefixing and the multipump constructor option), multi-step list writes for rate/volume/delay, startPump(multistep=True), and direct use of getResponse; the driver covers the single-pump, single-step commands. The raw reads pump_status, parameters and parameter_limits are the reply lines joined with a newline; the exact line layout and labels of the pump's replies are not modeled. The read-only displaced_volume and elapsed_time fields take the last number of their reply (the GUI reads the last token at CHEMYX_GUI.py:237); the clone states no unit for either, so both are published with the dimensionless UCUM unit 1. The rate, volume and time writes are sent verbatim in the unit selected by units, so their fields also carry unit 1. The diameter is mm and the delay is s (the GUI labels at CHEMYX_GUI.py:156,159). The five numeric writes are Limit.operator_required because no line of the clone states a range; site-limits.example.json is an example operator overlay, not a device fact. Risk is R2 above the card's R1 floor because the pump dispenses. The clone names no independent hardware emergency stop, so the R2 stop path (SAFE-045) is the safe-state action x-cap.cukelarter.stop.v1, which calls stopPump. The fake is an in-memory stand-in; its numbers are placeholders. The hardware backend imports core from the clone's python_dist/CHEMYX_python directory on PYTHONPATH and was never imported or run; no hardware was attached. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null). The gate was run three times: the first failed G2.BACKENDS_DIFFER, the second and third passed with the digest above and no warnings.
